sections.title: 一、詞彙題（占15分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1題至第15題，每題有4個選項，其中只有一個是正確或最適當的選項，請畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

questions.stem: Nowadays many companies adopt a ______ work schedule which allows their employees to decide when to arrive at work—from as early as 6 a.m. to as late as 11 a.m.
To teach children right from wrong, some parents will ______ their children when they behave well and punish them when they misbehave.
To stick to a tight budget, Robert bought a more ______ LED TV instead of a fancy, expensive 3D TV.
David’s new book made it to the best-seller list because of its beautiful ______ and amusing stories.
The airport was closed because of the snowstorm, and our ______ for Paris had to be delayed until the following day.
The moment the students felt the earthquake, they ran ______ out of the classroom to an open area outside.
The ______ capacity of this elevator is 400 kilograms. For safety reasons, it shouldn’t be overloaded.
An open display of ______ behavior between men and women, such as hugging and kissing, is not allowed in some conservative societies.
When taking medicine, we should read the instructions on the ______ carefully because they provide important information such as how and when to take it.
The angry passengers argued ______ with the airline staff because their flight was cancelled without any reason.
To ______ the new product, the company offered some free samples before they officially launched it.
I was worried about my first overseas trip, but my father ______ me that he would help plan the trip so that nothing would go wrong.
The recent cooking oil scandals have led to calls for tougher ______ of sales of food products.
John should ______ more often with his friends and family after work, instead of staying in his room to play computer games.
To prevent the spread of the Ebola virus from West Africa to the rest of the world, many airports have begun Ebola ______ for passengers from the infected areas.

sections.instructions: 說明︰第16題至第30題，每題一個空格，請依文意選出最適當的一個選項，請畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

Tai Chi Chuan is a type of ancient Chinese martial art. People [[16]] Tai Chi mainly for its health benefits. This centuries-old Chinese mind-body exercise is now gaining popularity in the United States.
The most familiar aspect of Tai Chi Chuan is the hand form, which is a series of slow-flowing movements with poetic names [[17]] “dragons stirring up the wind” and “wave hands like clouds.” These movements, forming an exercise system, [[18]] one to effortlessly experience the vital life force, or the Qi energy, in one’s body.
Tai Chi Chuan is not only a physical but also a [[19]] exercise. Psychologically, this exercise may increase communication between the body and the mind and enable one to deal with other people more effectively. It [[20]] stress and creates calmness and confidence. Relaxation and a feeling of joy are among the first noticeable differences in a Tai Chi student.

groups.passage: Much like the dove and robin, the bluebird is considered a very lucky sign in most cultures, particularly when seen in the spring. [[21]], a woodpecker, when seen near the home, is regarded as a good sign. In contrast, the peacock is not [[22]] seen as lucky. In places like India, the peacock is considered lucky because the great many “eyes” on its feathers are said to alert it to [[23]] evil. Peacocks are also highly valued in China and Japan, where they are kept as symbols by the ruling families to [[24]] their status and wealth. However, the peacock receives only scorn from the rest of the world. The feathers of peacocks are considered the most [[25]] part of the bird because the eye-shaped markings on them are associated with “evil eyes.” To bring the evil eye into the home is thus believed to invite trouble and sorrow.

Nutritional products that can be collected from trees include fruits, nuts, seeds, leaves, and bark. Tree products have been an important part of diets for thousands of years, from early humans [[26]] fruits and nuts to the first cultivation of important trees, such as mango and apple.
The apple is one of the world’s most cultivated fruit trees, [[27]] over 7,000 different kinds in existence. Despite their great [[28]], however, most domesticated apples can be traced back to a common ancestor, the wild apple of Central Asia, Malus sieversii. Apples have been grown for thousands of years in Asia and Europe, and [[29]] to North America by European colonists in the 17th century. sections.title: 三、文意選填（占10分）
sections.instructions: 說明：第31題至第40題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得1分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
A paperclip, made of steel wire bent into a hooped shape, is an instrument used to hold sheets of paper together. This common [[31]] is a wonder of simplicity and function. But where did this simple, cheap, and indispensable invention come from?
In the late 19th century, the most common way to hold papers together was by using a pin. Although the pin was an inexpensive tool and was easily [[32]], it would leave holes in the paper. Later, as steel wire became more common, inventors began to notice its elastic feature. With this feature, it could be stretched and [[33]] various clip-like objects. In the years just prior to 1900, quite a few paperclip designs emerged. The name most frequently [[34]] the paperclip invention is Johan Vaaler, a Norwegian inventor. However, Vaaler’s clips were not the same as the paperclips currently in use. Specifically, they did not have the interior loop we see today. The [[35]] looped design was invented by Gem Manufacturing Ltd. in England. This clip is therefore sometimes [[36]] the Gem clip.
Because of Vaaler, the paperclip played an important [[37]] role in Norway. During World War II, Norway was occupied by the Nazis. Norwegians were prohibited from wearing any [[38]] of their national unity, such as buttons with the initials of their king. Thus, in [[39]], they started wearing paperclips to show their solidarity. The reason for doing this was simple: Paperclips were a Norwegian invention whose original function was to bind together. After the war, a giant paperclip statue was erected in Oslo to [[40]] Vaaler—even though his design was never actually manufactured.

tags.topic: the invention and history of the paperclip

sections.title: 四、閱讀測驗（占32分）
sections.instructions: 說明︰第41題至第56題，每題請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個選項，請畫記在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。各題答對者，得2分；答錯、未作答或畫記多於一個選項者，該題以零分計算。

groups.passage:
In 2009, the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers were invited to perform in Belgium, France, Germany, and Luxemburg. In 2011, they were voted as one of the world’s top five performance groups by audiences of Japan Broadcasting Corporation’s Amazing Voice program.
Recalling the group’s first tour in Europe, Camake Valaule, a physical education teacher and the founder of the Taiwu Elementary School Folk Singers, admitted that he felt very nervous. He was worried that the audience would fall asleep since most of the 75-minute performance was a cappella, that is, singing without instrumental sound. Surprisingly, the audience listened with full focus and high spirits. Camake said, “They told me afterward that through our performance, they had a vision of our country, our village, without having to visit it. This experience greatly boosted our confidence.”
According to Camake Valaule, singing traditional ballads has helped students and their parents to re-understand their culture. “It used to be that the only ones who could sing these songs were tribal elders aged between 50 and 60. Now with the children performing the pieces, parents are beginning to ask, ‘Why do we not know how to sing these ballads?’ Many times nowadays, it is the children who teach the songs to their parents, putting back the pieces of a blurred memory.”
Winning international fame, however, was neither the original intention nor the main reason why Camake founded the group in 2006. The most important thing was to make children understand why they sing these songs and to preserve and pass on their culture. Referring to the relocation of Taiwu Elementary School and Taiwu Village following Typhoon Morakot in August 2009, Camake said, “We could not take the forest or our houses in the mountains with us; but we were able to bring our culture along. As long as the children are willing to sing, I will always be there for them, singing with them and leading them to experience the meaning of the ballads.”

options.A: The group was first established in 2009.
options.B: The group was founded by a PE teacher.

options.B: The fading memories about old tribal people.
options.C: The broken pieces of knowledge taught at school.

options.A: The significance of the relocation of Taiwu Elementary School.

options.C: The importance of passing on the traditional culture.
options.D: The consequence of building houses in the forest.

groups.passage:
When it comes to medical care, many patients and doctors believe “more is better.” But what they do not realize is that overtreatment—too many scans, too many blood tests, too many procedures—may pose harm. Sometimes a test leads you down a path to more and more testing, some of which may be invasive, or to treatment for things that should be left alone.
Terrence Power, for example, complained that after his wife learned she had Wegener’s disease, an uncommon disorder of the immune system, they found it difficult to refuse testing recommended by her physician. The doctor insisted on office visits every three weeks, even when she was feeling well. He frequently ordered blood tests and X-rays, and repeatedly referred her to specialists for even minor complaints. Even when tests came back negative, more were ordered, and she was hospitalized as a precaution when she developed a cold. She had as many as 25 doctor visits during one six-month period. The couple was spending about $30,000 a year for her care.
After several years of physical suffering and near financial ruin from the medical costs, the couple began questioning the treatment after consulting with other patients in online support groups. “It’s a really hard thing to determine when they’ve crossed the line,” Mr. Power said. “You think she’s getting the best care in the world, but after a while you start to wonder: What is the objective?” Mr. Power then spoke with his own primary care doctor, who advised him to find a new specialist to oversee Mrs. Power’s care. Under the new doctor’s care, the regular testing stopped and Mrs. Power’s condition stabilized. Now she sees the doctor only four or five times a year.

questions.stem: What is the main idea of this passage?

options.A: Treatments do not always cause harmful side effects.
options.B: Patients tend to believe more testing is better treatment.
options.C: Too much medical care may not be beneficial to patients.
options.D: Doctors generally recommend office visits that are necessary.

questions.stem: Which of the following was a problem for Mrs. Power during her medical treatment?

options.A: She had to be hospitalized for three weeks whenever she had a cold.
options.B: She didn’t have any insurance, so she went broke because of her illness.
options.C: When test results showed she was fine, her doctor still ordered more tests.
options.D: Her doctor asked her to consult other specialists due to her constant complaints.

questions.stem: Who does “they” in the third paragraph most likely refer to?
Which of the following best describes the author’s attitude toward medical tests?

options.A: More tests than necessary are too much.
options.B: Medical tests are essential for disease prevention.
options.C: Many tests are needed for confirmation of diagnosis.
options.D: Doctors’ interpretations of test results are seldom wrong.

groups.passage:
Henri Cartier-Bresson (1908–2004) is one of the most original and influential figures in the history of photography. His humane, spontaneous photographs helped establish photojournalism as an art form.
Cartier-Bresson’s family was wealthy—his father made a fortune as a textile manufacturer—but Cartier-Bresson later joked that due to his parents’ frugal ways, it often seemed as though his family was poor.
Educated in Paris, Cartier-Bresson developed an early love for literature and the arts. As a teenager, Cartier-Bresson rebelled against his parents’ formal ways of education. In his early adulthood, he even drifted toward communism. But it was art that remained at the center of his life.
Cartier-Bresson traveled to Africa in 1931 to hunt antelope and boar. And Africa fueled another interest in him: photography. He then wandered around the world with his camera, using a handheld camera to catch images from fleeting moments of everyday life.
Not long after World War II, Cartier-Bresson traveled east, spending considerable time in India, where he met and photographed Gandhi shortly before his assassination in 1948. Cartier-Bresson’s subsequent work to document Gandhi’s death and its immediate impact on the country became one of Life Magazine’s most prized photo essays.
Cartier-Bresson’s approach to photography remained much the same throughout his life. He made clear his dislike of images that had been improved by artificial light, darkroom effects, and even cropping. The naturalist in Cartier-Bresson believed that all editing should be done when the photo is taken. In 1952, his first book, The Decisive Moment, a rich collection of his work spanning two decades, was published. “There is nothing in this world that does not have a decisive moment,” he said.
In 1968, he began to turn away from photography and returned to his passion for drawing and painting.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes Cartier-Bresson’s family background?

options.A: His family was rich but was very economical.
options.B: His father went to Paris to open a textile factory.
options.C: His wealthy family went bankrupt and became poor.
options.D: His parents were very liberal in their ways of education.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about Cartier-Bresson’s career in photography?

options.B: He developed a passion for photography when he traveled to Africa.
options.C: He quit photography right after the publication of The Decisive Moment.
options.D: During World War II, he documented the everyday life of the Indian people.

questions.stem: What significance did Cartier-Bresson have to Gandhi of India?

options.B: He was the first photographer to take Gandhi’s photo.
options.C: He used photos to document the effect of Gandhi’s death on India.
options.D: His photos told the world who was guilty of assassinating Gandhi.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about Cartier-Bresson’s approach to photography?

options.A: He never waited for a decisive moment to shoot photos.
options.B: He preferred to edit his images carefully in his darkroom.
options.C: Most of his photos described things that happen every day.
options.D: He experimented with different ways and settled on being a naturalist.

groups.passage:
You’ve most likely heard the news by now: A car-commuting, desk-bound, TV-watching lifestyle can be harmful to our health. All the time that we spend rooted in the chair is linked to increased risks of so many deadly diseases that experts have named this modern-day health epidemic the “sitting disease.”
Sitting for too long slows down the body’s metabolism and the way enzymes break down our fat reserves, raising both blood sugar levels and blood pressure. Small amounts of regular activity, even just standing and moving around, throughout the day is enough to bring the increased levels back down. And those small amounts of activity add up—30 minutes of light activity in two or three-minute bursts can be just as effective as a half-hour block of exercise. But without that activity, blood sugar levels and blood pressure keep creeping up, steadily damaging the inside of the arteries and increasing the risk of diabetes, heart disease, stroke, and other serious diseases. In essence, fundamental changes in biology occur if you sit for too long.
But wait, you’re a runner. You needn’t worry about the harm of a sedentary lifestyle because you exercise regularly, right? Well, not so fast. Recent studies show that people spend an average of 64 hours a week sitting, whether or not they exercise 150 minutes a week as recommended by World Health Organization (WHO). Regular exercisers, furthermore, are found to be about 30 percent less active on days when they exercise. Overall, most people simply aren’t exercising or moving around enough to counteract all the harm that can result from sitting nine hours or more a day.
Scared straight out of your chair? Good. The remedy is as simple as standing up and taking activity breaks.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of this passage?

options.A: To point out the challenges of the modern lifestyle.
options.B: To discuss how a modern epidemic may spread quickly.
options.C: To explore the effects of regular exercise to our body.
options.D: To explain the threat to our health from long hours of sitting.

questions.stem: What does the word “sedentary” in the third paragraph most likely mean?
What is the best way to bring down high blood sugar level and blood pressure?

options.A: Exercising for 150 minutes or more every week.
options.B: Getting rid of the habit of car commuting and TV watching.
options.C: Interrupting sitting time with light activity as often as possible.
options.D: Standing or moving around for at least two or three minutes every day.

questions.stem: Which of the following may be inferred about those who do serious exercise?

options.A: They often live longer than those who don’t exercise.
options.B: They tend to stand or move around less on days they work out.
options.C: They generally spend less time sitting than those who are inactive.
options.D: They usually do not meet the standard of exercise recommended by WHO.

questions.label: 中譯英1
questions.stem: 一個成功的企業不應該把獲利當作最主要的目標。
questions.scoring_notes:
第一大題是「中譯英」，題型與過去幾年相同，考生需將兩個中文句子譯成正確、通順、達意的英文，兩題合計為 8 分。
評分標準與歷年相同，在「中譯英」部分，每小題總分 4 分，原則上是每個錯誤扣 0.5 分，相同的錯誤只扣一次。
今年的「中譯英」呼應最近社會發生的食安問題，提醒企業不應該以獲利為最主要目標，應該負起社會責任以增進大眾福祉，希望學生能以英文表達對社會現象的關心。評量的重點在於考生能否運用常用的詞彙與基本句型將兩句中文翻譯成正確、達意的英文句子，所測驗之句型為高中生熟悉的範圍，詞彙亦控制在大考中心詞彙表四級內之詞彙，中等程度以上的考生，如果能使用正確句型並注意用字、拼字，應能得理想的分數。例如：「不應該把獲利當作最主要的目標」若譯成 should not regard making profit as its primary goal 即可得分；「以增進大眾福祉」則可翻譯為 to enhance public/the public’s well-being/welfare 或者 to enhance the well-being/welfare of the public。在選取樣卷時，我們發現有不少考生對於英文詞彙的語意及使用，以及英文拼字仍有加強的空間，如第一句的「獲利」指的是企業的利潤應該是 profit(s)而不是 benefits；「福祉」應翻成 well-being/welfare，也不是 benefits；「最主要的目標」有考生翻譯為 the most main goal 重複了最高級的概念，多譯了 most；「成功的企業」中的「成功的」應為形容詞，有不少考生詞性用錯；「社會責任」social responsibilities 拼字錯誤的考生也不少，相當可惜。

figures.label: 兩本書的封面
figures.description: 題目下方並排畫著兩本立體書本（可見左側書脊與下方書頁），為黑白灰階圖。左邊一本：封面上方以粗體字印著書名「EVERYONE IS BEAUTIFUL:」，下一行為副標「Respect Others & Be Yourself」；中央是一棵枝葉茂盛的樹，樹幹中段印著作者名「Caroline Strong」，樹的下方有一個上下顛倒、逐漸淡出的倒影（像水中倒影）。右邊一本：封面上方是一組由左至右逐漸升高的長條形階梯（類似長條圖），最高的一根顏色最深，頂端架著一把往右上方延伸的梯子，一個小人正沿著梯子往上爬；下方以粗體字印著書名「LEADERSHIP IS A CHOICE:」，接著兩行副標「Conquer Your Fears &」「You Can Be a Leader Too」；最下方白色框內印著作者名「Austin Young」。

questions.label: 作文
questions.stem: 提示︰下面兩本書是學校建議的暑假閱讀書籍，請依書名想想看該書的內容，並思考你會選擇哪一本書閱讀，為什麼？請在第一段說明你會選哪一本書及你認為該書的內容大概會是什麼，第二段提出你選擇該書的理由。
questions.scoring_notes:
「英文作文」的評分標準是依據內容、組織、文法句構、詞彙拼字、體例五個項目給分，字數明顯不足的作文則扣總分 1 分。
第二大題是「英文作文」，以至少 120 個單詞，從兩本書當中選擇其中一本設想該書可能的內容，再說明為什麼選擇該本書的理由。
今年的「英文作文」主題是要考生從兩本書擇一作答，一本是 EVERYBODY IS BEAUTIFUL: Respect Others & Be Yourself，另外一本是 LEADERSHIP IS A CHOICE: Conquer Your Fears & You Can Be a Leader Too，考生要根據書名猜測該書的內容並說明為什麼選擇該本書，跳脫「看圖寫作」的模式。這種命題方式雖與過去四格漫畫敘述故事之方式不同，但本質仍為引導式寫作，以書名及副標作為提示，引導考生思考、寫作。題目要考生省思欣賞尊重他人，同時看重肯定自己，或者克服恐懼及培養領導能力的重要性，很符合社會對年輕人的正面期許。不論選擇哪本書，考生若能從不同的角度發揮想像力，清楚描述自己認為書中可能的內容，同時條理說明選擇的理由，就能拿到不錯的分數。評分的考量重點為作文內容與所選書籍之間關聯性是否緊密，並有足夠的細節支持，組織是否連貫合理，句構、語法及用字是否適切，以及拼字與標點符號是否正確得當。

extraction.method: 題本文字以 Word 版 paper-2.doc 為主（soffice --headless 轉成 docx 後，以 lxml 走訪 document.xml 的全部 w:r，底線 run 內的數字轉成 [[題號]]），再以程式將全部 278 個文字欄位（大題標題、說明、題組標示、選文各段、題幹、選項、選項庫）與 pdftotext -layout（paper-1.pdf）的詞序列逐段比對（英文比對連續詞序列、中文去空白後比對子字串），全部一致；Read 看 PDF 全部 8 頁頁面影像確認段落切分、粗體／斜體與底線，英文作文的兩本書封面另以 pdftoppm -r 300 放大裁切判讀；答案取自 answer.pdf（pdftotext -layout）；評分原則取自 scoring.pdf（pdftotext 與 -layout，並以 Read 看頁面影像核對）逐字摘錄；統計以 xlrd 讀 stats-1.xls（英文工作表：答對率 P、高分組 Ph、低分組 Pl、鑑別度 D）、stats-2.xls（英文工作表：選項分析 T／H／L 列、未答）、stats-3.xls（英文科非選擇題分數人數統計表），並以程式交叉核對（選項分析標 * 的選項＝官方答案；其 T 列比例＝P；H／L 列比例＝Ph／Pl（兩題差 1 個百分點，見 issues）；D＝Ph−Pl；非選擇題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數）。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat 期別「94–110」一致——詞彙題 1–15（15分）、綜合測驗 16–30（3篇×5題，題組標示16–20、21–25、26–30，15分）、文意選填 31–40（A–J，10分）、閱讀測驗 41–56（4篇×4題，每題2分，32分）、中譯英 2題×4分、英文作文 20分（文長至少120個單詞）；第壹部分單選題 72分＋第貳部分非選擇題 28分＝100分；封面「考試時間：100 分鐘」「單選題共 56 題」「非選擇題共二大題」。無差異。
validator warning「題號重複 [1, 2]」為預期：中譯英兩題題本編為 1.、2.，英文作文沒有題號（no 填 1）；no 必須是整數，故沿用題本編號，並以 label「中譯英1」「中譯英2」「作文」區分，label 無重複。

中譯英：評分原則沒有公布完整參考譯文，只舉出片段譯法（「不應該把獲利當作最主要的目標」若譯成 should not regard making profit as its primary goal 即可得分；「以增進大眾福祉」可譯為 to enhance public/the public’s well-being/welfare 或 to enhance the well-being/welfare of the public）與常見錯誤；這些不是整句譯文，故 answer 與 accepted_answers 皆為 null，片段譯法保留在 scoring_notes 原文中。評分原則的中譯英段落同時談兩句，無法逐句切開而不破壞原文，故兩題的 scoring_notes 都放：第一段「第一大題是「中譯英」…兩題合計為 8 分。」、評分標準句「評分標準與歷年相同…相同的錯誤只扣一次。」、整段中譯英說明（逐字），以換行分隔。
英文作文：評分原則沒有官方範文，answer 為 null。scoring_notes 由評分原則三處逐字摘錄組成（「英文作文」評分標準句、第一段中「第二大題是「英文作文」，以至少 120 個單詞…理由。」、最後一段作文說明），以換行分隔。本年評分項目為五項（內容、組織、文法句構、詞彙拼字、體例），與 spec 所記 106 年起才改為四項一致。
英文作文 tags：題目以兩本書的封面（書名＋副標）為提示，要求第一段說明選哪一本書及推想的內容、第二段說明理由；評分原則明言「跳脫「看圖寫作」的模式…本質仍為引導式寫作，以書名及副標作為提示」，故 essay_type 標 topic（與 gsat-107／108 同為指定兩段內容的主題寫作；也可視為 two_paragraph），paragraphs=2。
書名差異：題本封面圖上的左邊書名為「EVERYONE IS BEAUTIFUL: Respect Others & Be Yourself」（300dpi 影像確認），評分原則則寫作「EVERYBODY IS BEAUTIFUL: Respect Others & Be Yourself」。依逐字原則，figure 描述照題本封面，scoring_notes 照評分原則原文，兩者都不改。
英文作文圖（s6g1 figures）：兩本書封面只以圖片呈現，Word 版與 PDF 文字層都沒有封面上的文字；封面文字（書名、副標、作者 Caroline Strong／Austin Young）依 300dpi 頁面影像逐字抄錄，圖案（樹與倒影、逐漸升高的長條階梯與梯子上攀爬的小人）以文字描述。

選擇題統計：stats-2.xls 選項分析與 stats-1.xls 有兩處相差 1 個百分點（兩張表各自四捨五入）：第16題 L 列正答 A 為 36%，stats-1 的 Pl 為 35%；第32題 H 列正答 D 為 87%，stats-1 的 Ph 為 86%。兩者都照原表保留（high_group／low_group 取 stats-1，option_rates_high／option_rates_low 取 stats-2），stats-1 的 D＝Ph−Pl 全部 56 題成立。其餘已程式核對：選項分析中標 * 的選項＝官方答案（56 題全部），T 列正答比例＝P。各題 option_rates（加未答）因四捨五入加總為 0.98–1.02（第32題 T 1.02、L 0.98；第34題 L 1.02；第40題 T 0.98；第46題 L 0.98）。
選擇題統計：除 schema 欄位外，另存 option_rates_high／option_rates_low（stats-2.xls 選項分析的高分組 H、低分組 L 列）與 omit_rate（全體未答比例，T 列；本年只有第56題 T 列未答 1%）；stats-1.xls 的五組通過率 Pa–Pe 與 D1–D4 未收錄。

非選擇題統計：stats-3.xls 只有「第一題（中譯英，滿分8分，兩小題合計）」與「第二題（英文作文，滿分20分）」的分數人數分布，無法拆到中譯英各小題，因此放在 sections[s5].stats 與 sections[s6].stats 的 score_distribution（schema 未定義此欄位，沿用 gsat-106／107／109 的做法）；rate 為原表百分比÷100，分母是報名人數 146,035（含缺考 2,152；到考 143,883），已核對兩題各分數段人數加總＝到考人數 143,883。原表分數區間「9.00- 9.99」等的空白已去除；第一題 8 分以上的列在原表為空白，未收錄。小題層級 stats 為 null。

低答對率／低鑑別度題目已複核非對齊錯誤（皆為大考中心原始數據）：第15題 P=0.28、D=0.18（41% 選 D blockings）；第13題 P=0.40、D=0.30（33% 選 B guarantee）；第18題 P=0.33（44% 選 D allowing）；第23題 P=0.36、D=0.24（47% 選 A approach，高分組 A 47%／B 49%）；第30題 P=0.40、D=0.34；第39題 P=0.33（21% 選 B honor）；第34題 P=0.38（30% 選 E known as）；第54題 P=0.36、D=0.32；第56題 P=0.36、D=0.32；第52題 D=0.32。

格式：題本中第41–44題選文與第43題的 the pieces of a blurred memory、第45–48題選文與第47題的 they、第53–56題選文與第54題的 sedentary 為粗體；第26–30題選文的 Malus sieversii、第49–52題選文的 Life Magazine 與 The Decisive Moment（含第50題 (C)）為斜體；19th、17th 的 th 為上標；「第16至20題為題組」等題組標示有底線。依 schema 不保留粗斜體（題目以引號指稱，非「畫底線的字」，故未加 <u>）。

逐字保留的原文寫法：第41–44題選文 Luxemburg（常見拼法為 Luxembourg，Luxemburg 為較舊／德文拼法）；第53–56題選文「Small amounts of regular activity, even just standing and moving around, throughout the day is enough…」（主詞複數、動詞 is）與「as recommended by World Health Organization (WHO)」（無冠詞 the）；第53題 (C)「the effects of regular exercise to our body」。皆照題本，未更正。

文字來源：Word 版第41–44題選文第2、3段被放在同一個段落（中間以換行分隔），依 PDF 版面拆成兩段；選文共 4 段。PDF 選項庫印作「(F) protest」「( I ) associated with」「( J ) historical」（括號內有空白），代號統一為 F／I／J。第21、28、32、39題空格後的逗號依題本緊接空格（例「[[21]], a woodpecker」「great [[28]], however」）。第12題 Word 版題幹中有一個粗體空白 run，不影響文字。

評分原則 PDF：pdftotext 把「以增進大眾福祉」的「福祉」輸出成「福 祉」（跨行時的字距），頁面影像上沒有空白，已改為「福祉」；跨行接合時，前後都是英文或數字的位置補一個空白（例「or to / enhance」「EVERYBODY / IS」「扣總分 / 1 分」），中文與全形標點處直接接合（例「well-being/welfare」＋「，也不是 benefits」）。評分原則與題本文字經 NFC 正規化前後相同（無 CJK 相容表意字）。

標註判斷：第44題（Camake 在莫拉克颱風後體悟到什麼）答案需由引言「We could not take the forest… but we were able to bring our culture along」推得，標 inference；第43、47題依 repo 慣例（What does “…” refer to）標 reference；s4g1 為附直接引語的人物報導，genre 標 news，sdgs 標 [4, 11]（文化多樣性教育、文化資產保存）；第27題「with over 7,000 different kinds in existence」標 grammar／with_absolute_construction（沿用其他年份的 grammar_point 名稱）。

本檔新增的非 schema 欄位：section.part_title／part_instructions（第壹、貳部分標題與第貳部分共同說明，放在該部分的第一個大題 s1、s5）、section.stats（非選擇題分數分布）、group.group_label（「第16至20題為題組」等題本原文）、figure.label、sources.paper_word、question.stats.option_rates_high／option_rates_low／omit_rate。
